sentences.text:
Shree Vardhman Parivar vs The State Of West Bengal And
Others on 29 October, 2025
October 29, 2025
Sl. No.65
Court No.1
s.biswas
 Wpa(P) 427 of 2025
 Shree Vardhman Parivar
 vs.
 The State of West Bengal and others
 Mr. Vinay Kr. Sharaff

Mr. Dev Kr. Agarwal
 Ms. Swarnwarshi Poddar

... for the petitioner
 Mr. Kishore Datta, Ag
 Ms. Sumita Shaw
 Mr. Soumen Chatterjee
 ... for the State
 Mr. Kalyan Kumar Chakraborty
 Mr. Gopal Krishna Sarkar
 Dr. Benoy Brata Bhowmik
 ... for the respondent no.5
1.
Mr. Vinay Kr. Sharaff, learned counsel for the petitioner, Ms. Sumita Shaw, learned counsel for the State and Mr. Kalyan Kumar Chakraborty, learned counsel for the respondent no.5 are present.

Nobody appeared for the respondent no.2.
2.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that this petition is filed to prevent illegal sacrifice of animals.

By taking this court to a report (Annexure P-14) by a committee constituted by Supreme Court in WP(C) 881 of 2014, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the Chief Secretary of the State of West Bengal was also a party.

Reliance is placed on Clause 5 of the said report which reads thus:
"5) Restriction on slaughter:
Apart from focusing on Gadhimai alone, which happens once in 5 years, all the small animal sacrifice events may also be summarily discouraged and illegal slaughter of animals prevented by the State Govts. and their agencies.
This way a solid platform and precedence can be built before the next Gadhimai event.
No animal slaughter may be allowed at any religious or public place and slaughter may be permitted only in accordance with the Food Safety and Standards Act 2006 and Regulations 2011."

3. It is further submitted by learned counsel for the petitioner that the said report, pursuant to a joint meeting of the respondent State, was placed before the Supreme Court on 13.07.2015 in WP(C)

1 881 of 2014.

entities.text: Shree Vardhman Parivar vs The State Of West Bengal And Others on 29 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Apex Court recorded that the said decision formulated by all the respondents deserves to be accepted.
All the State Governments were directed to submit compliance report to the Apex Court before 16.11.2015.
Reliance is also placed on the order dated 04.07.2016 of Supreme Court in the case wherein State of West Bengal also submitted its affidavit.
The Apex Court opined that the only deficiency appears to be in framing the rules under Section 38 of the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act.

entities.text: Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The said writ petition was disposed of on 12th July, 2016 by observing that draft rules under the act should be finalized within three months.

4. The learned counsel for the petitioner by placing reliance on the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Slaughter House) Rules, 2001 submits that animals cannot be slaughtered except in the manner prescribed in this Rules.

entities.text: Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Slaughter House) Rules, 2001
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: By placing heavy reliance on Rule 3 of the said Rules, it is submitted that slaughter of animals is permissible only in the slaughter house recognized or licensed by the concerned authority empowered under the law.
Sub-Rule 3 of Rule 3 further makes it clear that number of animals to be slaughtered in a day has to be determined by the concerned municipal/local authority.
5. In the instant case, the sacrifice of the animals at the puja pandals which runs contrary to the Rules of 2001.
Such sacrifice is totally impermissible and runs contrary to the spirit of the orders of the Supreme Court and the statutory mandate engraved in the Rules of 2001.
6. Learned counsel for the State submits that the State has already formed a committee to ensure that illegal slaughter does not take place.
She prays for a day's time to seek instruction and apprise this court in this regard.

7. The State Government is directed to seek instruction whether animal sacrifice in case of this nature falls within the ambit of "prohibited practices" as defined in Rule 2(t) of the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act.

entities.text: Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The State shall further apprise whether Rule 10 of the Rules of 2023, the aforesaid can be pressed into service by imposing penalty for contravention of rules.
8. The respondent no.5 may also argue the matter on the next day.
9. Considering the fact that the puja is scheduled on 7th November, 2025, as agreed, list this matter on Friday i.e. on 31st October, 2025.

(Sujoy Paul, A.C.J.) (Smita Das De, J.)
